subject: Life Skills
title: Automating Your Finances
description: A micro-lesson that makes Automating Your Finances usable.

hook.text: He planned to save $500 a month. Every month, something came up. After a year, his savings account held $200.

buildup.text: Manual saving relies on willpower. Willpower is limited and decays. Automation removes the human from the failure point.

discovery.text: Set up auto-transfers on payday: savings first, bills second, spending last. This is 'pay yourself first' in practice.

twist.text: People who automate savings save 80% more than those who do it manually.

climax.text: Automate bills too. Late fees alone cost the average American $150 per year. Automation kills that cost entirely.

punchline.text: Automate everything. Willpower is too expensive.

quiz.question: Why is automated saving more effective than manual saving?
options: Banks offer higher interest rates for automated accounts
It removes the need for willpower, which degrades over time
